name.baseName: Heat from waste, at municipal waste incineration plant

dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: The multioutput-process 'municipal solid waste to municipal incineration' delivers the co-products 'disposal, municipal solid waste, 22.9% water, to municipal incineration' and 'electricity from waste, at municipal waste incineration plant' and 'heat from waste, at municipal waste incineration plant '. Default allocation 100% to disposal function, 0% to energy production. These allocation factors also apply to emissions of waste heat: i.e. neither electricity nor heat from waste at MSWI does contain any waste heat emissions. Inventoried waste contains 21% paper; 8% Mixed cardbord; 15% plastics; 3% laminated materials; 2% laminated packaging, e.g. tetra bricks; 3% combined goods: dipers; 3% glass; 2% textiles; 8% minerals; 9% natural products; 22% compostable material; 2.65% inert metals; 1% volatile metals; 0.0065% batteries; 0.34% electronic goods; . waste composition (wet, in ppm): upper heating value 13.27 MJ/kg; lower heating value 11.74 MJ/kg; H2O 228830; O 257060; H 48250; C 334230; S 1119; N 3123.8; P 893.79; B 7.1933; Cl 6866.2; Br 13.552; F 56.358; I 0.0121; Ag 0.714; As 0.62521; Ba 149.04; Cd 11.748; Co 1.3453; Cr 315.21; Cu 1212.8; Hg 1.4424; Mn 259.36; Mo 1.9551; Ni 107.38; Pb 502.43; Sb 22.564; Se 0.31969; Sn 73.44; V 9.2147; Zn 1311.2; Be n.a.; Sc n.a.; Sr n.a.; Ti n.a.; Tl n.a.; W n.a.; Si 48510; Fe 29996; Ca 14062; Al 12420; K 2059.7; Mg 3377.7; Na 5143.9; Share of carbon in waste that is biogenic 60.4%. Share of iron in waste that is metallic/recyclable 60%. Net energy produced in MSWI: 1.01MJ/kg waste electric energy and 2.16MJ/kg waste electric energy Allocation of energy production: no substitution or expansion. Total burden allocated to waste disposal function of MSWI. One kg of this waste produces 0.1888 kg of slag and 1 kg of residues, which are landfilled. ;; UUID: cc476d2d-20a3-3064-a77e-8d173cc5ac5e

time.common:timeRepresentativenessDescription: Waste composition as given in literature reference, theoretical data or other source. Transfer coefficients for modern Swiss MSWI. Emission speciation based on early 90ies data.

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: Specific to the technology mix encountered in Switzerland in 2000. Well applicable to modern incineration practices in Europe, North America or Japan.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
average Swiss MSWI plants in 2000 with electrostatic precipitator for fly ash (ESP), wet flue gas scrubber and 29.4%, SNCR 32.2%, SCR-high dust 24.6%, SCR-low dust DeNOx facilities and 13.8% without Denox (by burnt waste, according to Swiss average). Share of waste incinerated in plants with magnetic scrap separation from slag : 50%. Gross electric efficiency technology mix 12.997% and Gross thermal efficiency technology mix 25.57%

# Included processes
waste-specific air and water emisions from incineration, auxiliary material consumption for flue gas cleaning. Short-term emissions to river water and long-term emisisons to ground water from slag compartment (from bottom slag) and residual material landfill (from solidified fly ashes and scrubber slugde). Process energy demands for MSWI.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.samplingProcedure: waste-specific calculation based on literature data

review.common:reviewDetails: Proof reading validation: Passed. Total waste heat minus the energy in net produced electricity (if any) is completely allocated to the waste disposal function. No burdens are allocated to energy production (electricity nor heat).; Other validation: none;
